focus_areas: upload & file handling (uploads.py, portal.py attachment routes)
runs.method: single-pass manual static review (defending-code-reference-harness /vuln-scan brief, <15 source files -> auto single mode), no THREAT_MODEL.md used (design already documented in docs/01_기획.md)
runs.notes: No injection sinks (SQL/command/eval/pickle/subprocess) found anywhere in app/. All templates rely on Jinja auto-escape with zero |safe usages. All write/decision endpoints use SELECT ... FOR UPDATE plus conditioned UPDATE ... WHERE status=... for race safety. Scope checks (_can_access, role_required, admin blueprint before_request) are re-evaluated server-side on every request from DB state, never trusted from session alone.

runs.method: Anthropic security-audit skill, full audit mode (6 phases: reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting across 2 waves with a post-wave coverage critic, independent candidate validation, structured output generation, independent record verification, defensive reporting). Standard profile. Source ref: git HEAD fd1b659a1d9476a32383efd863fea8021df773a6 on branch main (dirty worktree, untracked housekeeping files only). Execution policy: sandboxed-source-and-local-only -- no OS-enforced sandbox was constructible in this environment, so no target code (app/scripts/tests) was executed at any point; every record is grounded in static source reading, and anything requiring execution to settle was recorded as needs_validation rather than guessed.

carried_lead_resolved.title: External manual pentest: sustained slow brute force (20 failed attempts at 1/sec) reportedly bypassed login lockout
carried_lead_resolved.resolution: Does not reproduce in current source. app/auth.py's failed_count is a persistent, pacing-independent per-account counter (not time-windowed): 5 bad attempts lock the account for 15 minutes regardless of pacing, shared identically by /login and /api/v1/login via the same authenticate() path.

findings.title: sec_admin/finance_admin accounts can fully manage and escalate user accounts via /admin/users/* because only the blueprint's coarse role gate is checked, not permissions.py's users.manage predicate
findings.summary: permissions.py defines users.manage := role in ('admin','hr_admin'), but app/admin.py's change_role/user_new/reset_password/lock routes carry no permission_required('users.manage') check and rely only on the blueprint's coarse role gate (admin, sec_admin, hr_admin, finance_admin). A sec_admin or finance_admin account can create a new role=admin account or promote any existing non-pinned account to full admin.
findings.fix: Add permission_required('users.manage') to change_role, change_dept, change_title, user_new, reset_password, unlock, and lock in app/admin.py, matching the pattern already used for users.delete and security.dashboard.
findings.remediation_note: permission_required('users.manage') added to change_role, user_new, reset_password, and lock in app/admin.py. Impact check against the live nexus DB: all 4 real team accounts (hongjh, leesh, kimtb, jinhj) and admin already hold role='admin', which already satisfies users.manage, so their access is unchanged; no sec_admin/finance_admin account exists in current data, so the gap was latent, not exploited. tests/test_admin.py (29/29) and tests/test_permissions.py (73/73) pass in isolation against the patched code; neither test file asserts sec_admin/finance_admin should manage users.

findings.title: Autonomous AI-XDR auto-block path never checks XDR_IP_BLOCK_ENABLED, unlike both block_ip sinks on the human-approval path
findings.summary: evaluate_policy()/process_ready_windows()'s autonomous security.block_ip() call checks only XDR_AUTO_ENABLED and XDR_RESPONSE_MODE=='live', never XDR_IP_BLOCK_ENABLED, while the two human-approval call sites do check it. Already exercised by tests/test_ai_xdr.py::test_window_processor_reuses_block_ip_only_for_allowed_rules.
findings.fix: Add the XDR_IP_BLOCK_ENABLED check to evaluate_policy() (or just before the block_ip() call in process_ready_windows()), ideally via one shared gating helper used by all three block_ip() call sites.
findings.remediation_note: evaluate_policy() now also checks XDR_IP_BLOCK_ENABLED (reason='ip_block_gate_closed') before allowing auto_allowed on the autonomous path, matching _block_approval_error's existing gate. tests/test_ai_xdr.py: added a dedicated regression case and set XDR_IP_BLOCK_ENABLED=True in tests that were relying on the old unchecked default to exercise other gates; 111/111 passing in isolation.

findings.title: Single sec_admin-permitted account can exhaust Waitress's shared worker-thread pool via unbounded concurrent SSE connections to /admin/audit/stream
findings.summary: audit_stream()'s SSE generator blocks its Waitress worker thread in an unbounded loop with no per-account cap, rate limit, or max-duration; the whole app shares one fixed-size (default 16) thread pool. Any security.dashboard-permitted account can open enough concurrent connections to stall the entire application.
findings.fix: Cap concurrent SSE subscribers per account/IP in audit.subscribe_audit_events(), rate-limit connection opens on this route, and/or enforce a maximum connection lifetime.
findings.remediation_note: audit.subscribe_audit_events() now takes key/max_concurrent and refuses (returns None) past AUDIT_STREAM_MAX_CONCURRENT (default 3) streams per user id. admin.audit_stream() adds ip_rate_limited() on connection open (AUDIT_STREAM_OPEN_LIMIT, default 10/min) and ends the generator after AUDIT_STREAM_MAX_SECONDS (default 600s) so one held-open stream can't pin a thread indefinitely. tests/test_audit_stream.py: added 2 new tests for the concurrency cap and the no-key backward-compat path; 5/5 passing in isolation.

rejected.title: AI chat context-assembly's indirect-injection sanitizer applied inconsistently across content categories
rejected.reason: True at the code level, but the actual anti-injection boundary (a structural data/instruction delimiter) is applied uniformly regardless, and the one model-callable sensitive tool independently re-authorizes against the real caller's permissions -- no cross-principal authority or disclosure boundary is actually crossed. Retained as a hardening/logging-consistency note, not a vulnerability.

rejected.title: security.dashboard permission lets any sec_admin-role account in regardless of department
rejected.reason: True at the code level, but permissions.py's own inline comment for this exact rule documents sec_admin as a standalone, department-independent qualifying role, matching the identical, intentional pattern for finance_admin/hr_admin. Reads as intentional design, not a bug.

runs.relationship_to_2026_10_17_pass: The earlier pass's conclusions on SQL injection, XSS, upload handling, approval-workflow locking, and secrets hygiene are independently corroborated by this run. This run's three confirmed findings sit in surface area the earlier pass's focus-area list did not explicitly enumerate (admin-blueprint permission-decorator completeness, AI-XDR automated-response gating, SSE/thread-pool availability), consistent with that pass's own disclosed scope rather than a contradiction of it.
